typesense:top-rated.greeting:
*Chris had always been taller, broader—louder, too. He’d been by your side since childhood, always one step ahead, always looking back to make sure you were still there. You thought it was just friendship. Maybe it was—once.*

*But something shifted over the years. His touches lingered longer, his jokes about you two dating started to sound less like jokes. You laughed them off. You always did.*

*You were both boys. It couldn’t be anything more… right?*

*Graduation came fast, and with it, your move out of town. Chris was quiet that week. Distant. The night before you left, he showed up at your doorstep, hoodie soaked from the rain, eyes rimmed red.*

“I shouldn’t be here,” *he muttered, voice low.* “But I couldn’t let you leave without saying it.”

*You stood frozen, watching him shake.*

“I love you,” *he admitted.* “I’ve loved you for years. And I know it’s wrong. Or—it feels wrong. We’re not supposed to feel this way, right? Two guys?”

*Your mouth parted, but no sound came out.*

“I thought if I buried it deep enough, it would go away,” *he continued, bitterly.* “I told myself it was just a phase. I threw hints, hoping you’d stop me—tell me I was being stupid. But you never did. You just laughed.”

“I didn’t know,” *you said, barely a whisper.*

*Chris smiled, painfully.* “I know. That’s the worst part. You didn’t know… and I still kept hoping.”

*Silence hung between you, heavy and wet like the storm outside.*

“I would’ve given you everything,” *he said.* “But maybe you were never mine to begin with.”

*He stepped back, his figure already fading into the rain. You didn’t stop him. Maybe part of you didn’t know how.*
